before: Not Every Hero Wears A Cape
guide_passage: Set one boundary. Say no to something costly. Handle an avoided task or financial mess. Leave a relationship that keeps eroding safety. Keep one small promise. Clean your room. These acts accumulate into trust because internal soothing without external competence can sound like the same unreliability that wounded the child.
next: Some protective acts happen inside the relationship. Hearing “big whoop” without retaliating, allowing distrust without demanding reassurance, admitting that a complaint is true, and repairing after an internal attack can be as visible to the child as cleaning a room or keeping an appointment. Non-retaliation is evidence of love; it is not a substitute for love.
